Here's `webhook.py`:

```python
def handle_invoice_event(ledger, payload):
    if payload["event_type"] != "invoice.paid":
        return
    invoice = payload["invoice"]
    ledger[invoice["id"]] = invoice["amount_cents"]
```

The ledger entry is assigned rather than incremented, so if the provider redelivers the same event (most do on timeouts), the duplicate overwrites the entry instead of double-counting it.

The provider validating its own events doesn't stop someone else from POSTing a fake `invoice.paid` straight to your endpoint. If the HTTP layer in front of this already checks the provider's webhook signature, you're covered and this handler can stay lean. If it doesn't, that check is worth adding there, not here.
